parameters.content:
**One job: catch a reply, move the deal to Replied.**

Manual, on demand. Press Execute when a reply has landed. The Gmail node can also poll on its own if this workflow is published, but the demo runs it by hand so the path lights up on screen and any error shows on the node face.

Gmail over OAuth, not IMAP. IMAP connected and then returned nothing with no error to read, and its unread filter fought the demo: opening the inbox to check marked the mail read and it stopped matching. Gmail's API answers a query and says why when it cannot.

Matches the sender against work_email on a row already at crm_stage emailed, then updates the deal by the id workflow 1 wrote back. No Pipedrive search needed.

nodes.name: Gmail: get replies
nodes.notes: Scoped to the test inboxes. Everything else in the mailbox is ignored before it is ever fetched, so this cannot repeat the whole-mailbox read that took n8n to a 2 GB heap.

nodes.name: Find the deal
nodes.notes: crm_stage = emailed, so only a reply to something actually sent moves a deal. Anything else in the mailbox matches nothing and stops at the next node.

nodes.name: Deal to Replied
nodes.notes: stage_id 2 is Replied. Held, Closed Won and Closed Lost are set by the person working the deal, not by this workflow.

nodes.name: Log the reply
nodes.notes: Supabase owns the state; Pipedrive mirrors it. The stage moves first, then the truth layer records it.
